business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

US-Luxembourg Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996), as amended by the 2009 Protocol
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty program (93+ active BITs)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as amended by the Loi du 25 juin 2020; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO Register Law), as amended; Règlement grand-ducal du 10 janvier 2019 fixing the operating modalities of the UBO register; CSSF Règlement 12-02 du 14 décembre 2012, as amended; Loi du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales, as amended, in particular by the Loi du 10 août 2016 modernising the SARL; Loi du 31 mai 1999 sur la domiciliation de sociétés, as amended

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the country of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of each corporate shareholder approving the incorporation, capital contribution, and appointment of managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or residential lease) for each individual UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or landlord in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional curriculum vitae and police clearance certificate of each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal or national police/criminal records authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every shareholder, UBO, manager, director, authorized signatory and material counterparty against: (i) the consolidated EU CFSP financial sanctions list; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Luxembourg national sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance; (iv) OFAC SDN/SSI and country-specific lists, mandatory because the target payment rails are USD-denominated SWIFT wires and standby letters of credit; (v) FATF and EU lists of high-risk third countries; and (vi) domestic PEP indicators under FATF Recommendation 12 and Directive (EU) 2018/843. The UBO declaration must be filed with the Luxembourg register of effective beneficiaries before or concurrently with incorporation. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to any PEP, corporate shareholder with bearer shares, nominee arrangement, or high-risk geographic nexus. Ongoing monitoring is continuous, with mandatory re-screening at least every 12 months and immediate re-screening upon any material change in ownership, management, or sanctions status.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - https://www.lbr.lu (e-RCS online filing and name reservation interface)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The articles of association and registration filings must be drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish; if another language is used, a sworn French translation is required. The company name must be written in Latin characters and must be distinguishable from existing registered corporate names and from names that may cause confusion with trademarks or natural persons. A Société à Responsabilité Limitée must include the suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' in its corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Caisse de retraite / Pension fund (requires CAA authorization)
Fonds / Fund / OPCVM / UCITS (requires CSSF authorization)
État / State / Municipal / Commune (implies public authority, requires ministerial clearance)
Luxembourg (when used to imply governmental or institutional affiliation)
Université / Hospital / Red Cross / Chamber of Commerce (sensitive institutional tokens requiring prior consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a requested name by the RCS through the e-RCS portal, the applicant may either file a new reservation with a revised name or, within 40 days from the notification of the refusal, file an administrative appeal with the Minister of Justice (Ministère de la Justice) stating the legal grounds for availability. A further judicial challenge lies before the Administrative Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal administratif) within 3 months of the administrative decision, supported by a written legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel. During the appeal procedure the applicant may provisionally re-reserve a modified name to avoid loss of time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is accepted only in the regulated form of commercial domiciliation through an RCS-approved domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999. For this bunkering entity, a pure virtual office without any local staff, records, or management infrastructure is not recommended: the VAT registration, excise and customs supervision, fuel bunkering licensing, and the banks that will issue or confirm standby letters of credit will require genuine administrative and operational substance. The registered office must be a real street address in Luxembourg at which legal process and official service of documents can be reliably received.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability within the first 12 months of operation. The risk is elevated because marine fuel bunkering is excise-sensitive and customs-controlled, and the CRF (financial intelligence unit), customs authorities, VAT authorities, and the RCS may conduct unannounced on-site inspections to verify the existence of substance and registered office. Use of a domiciliation address increases the inspection probability.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per document; estimated 6-8 documents at EUR 20-40 each

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation of foreign documents and of the draft articles of association into French

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg avocat pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing analysis, AML/CFT compliance advice, and legal opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the company in the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the deed of incorporation in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee of approximately EUR 75

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing and processing of the UBO declaration with the Luxembourg register of effective beneficiaries (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Minister of Finance / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory handling fee of EUR 30 plus professional service charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 150-250 per month depending on scope of services (mail handling, telephone, compliance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of EUR 30-80 per extract plus postage and apostille where required

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Consolidated Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Part III on the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), Articles 100-1 et seq.; in particular the provisions on minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, paid-up contribution rules, registered office, and appointment of managers (gérants); together with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and annual accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); notarial e-filing through the eRCS online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarised deed of incorporation) together with the statuts coordonnés (coordinated articles of association), filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL requires a minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed at incorporation. At least 25% of the par value of each cash-funded share must be paid up at subscription, collected in the notary's blocked client account and released after RCS registration. In-kind contributions must be fully paid at incorporation and supported by the statutory auditor's report; no separate escrow bank account is statutorily required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS AND DESIGNATED MANAGER OF [COMPANY NAME] S.À R.L.
Resolved: (1) The share subscription list is approved; the share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed, and each subscriber has paid at least 25% of the subscribed amount into the notary's blocked client account for release after RCS registration. (2) The registered office of the company is adopted at [full address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, where all statutory registers will be kept. (3) [Name] is appointed manager (gérant), with signature authority, empowered to open bank accounts, file RCS and RES filings, and apply for all commercial, environmental and marine bunkering licences. (4) The manager is authorised to execute all ancillary documents and to comply with corporate governance obligations. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name pre-clearance and incorporator due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via a Luxembourg notary; RCS pre-approval interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names to the notary for availability and distinctness screening against the RCS database. Verify the identity, legal capacity, beneficial ownership and good standing of each incorporator. If a name is unavailable, select the next preference before preparing the deed.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names
Passport or national identity document of each incorporator
Proof of residential or business address
Power of attorney for any legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or misleading, the notary resubmits an alternative cleared name; an amended draft may be prepared without repeating prior verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of incorporation documents and collection of subscribed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and Luxembourg credit institution holding the blocked client account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary prepares the draft deed of incorporation and coordinated articles, including the corporate objects covering marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment, capital structure, registered office, manager powers, financial year, and audit waiver. Each subscriber transfers at least 25% of the subscribed nominal amount into the notary's blocked client account; the notary obtains a bank confirmation of received funds and matches them to the subscription schedule. For in-kind contributions, the entire asset must be transferred and a statutory auditor's valuation report is attached.
required_dossiers: Draft coordinated articles of association
Shareholders' identity documents
Criminal record certificate or equivalent for each proposed manager
Capital payment instructions
Bank transfer confirmation or bank statement proving credited funds
Statutory auditor's in-kind valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the funds are incomplete or not properly referenced, the notary requests a corrected transfer or SWIFT reference; the notarial signature session is postponed until the bank confirmation shows the required paid-in capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarisation of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Notariat, authorised notary office in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the notarial signature session, each incorporator appears personally or by authenticated power of attorney. The notary verifies legal capacity, reads the deed, confirms that the minimum capital payment has been made, accepts the signatures, and authenticates the acte constitutif. The notary retains the original and prepares the electronic RCS filing package.
required_dossiers: Final text of the incorporation deed and coordinated articles
Bank or notary attestation of paid-up capital
Proof of identity of each signatory
Power of attorney for any absent shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder cannot attend or a legal formality remains outstanding, the notary schedules a replacement session and reserves the text; the RCS filing occurs only after all signatures and capital confirmations are complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), eRCS platform of Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the signed deed, coordinated articles, manager appointment declaration, corporate governance data, and capital attestation through the eRCS channel. The RCS examines formal legality, assigns the RCS registration number, and grants legal personality from the moment of registration.
required_dossiers: Notarised incorporation deed
Coordinated articles of association
RCS Form A or official e-filing form
Statutory declaration of the appointed manager
Bank or notary attestation of paid-up capital
Consent to act as manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR raises a query, the notary submits a formal explanation and any missing attachments; if the deed contains an incurable defect, a rectification deed is executed and the corrected file is resubmitted, normally within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and issuance of official RCS extracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, the RCS publishes the legal notice in the RES. The company obtains a certified RCS extract and certificate of incorporation for bank account opening, counterparty verification, and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number or e-file reference
Copy of the registered incorporation deed
Power of attorney for extract request, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or the text is erroneous, the notary files a correction request with the LBR; the published extract is reissued with the corrected wording at no additional fee.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; primary digital portal: MyGuichet.lu and guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first complete commercial registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR). Following RCS clearance, the SARL must apply to the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for Luxembourg VAT identification, and to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate tax file opening and income tax identification. A local tax representative is ordinarily required for non-resident entities making taxable supplies in Luxembourg. The application requires the global ultimate beneficial owner details, RCS extraction, constitutive deed of the SARL, and evidence of business activity (including the statutory license for marine fuel bunkering issued under the Luxembourg maritime / logistics licensing regime). The VAT number and national TIN are issued in official communication from AEDT and ACD, respectively. Registration must be completed before commencing taxable supplies; a registration application can be made by mail, via a Luxembourg-based professional (titre professionnel or certified accountant), or via a notarial filing where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Luxembourg SARL is resident and fiscally opaque, subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax on its worldwide income, subject to territoriality sourced-income modifications, tax treaties, and participation exemption. The SARL is not a pass-through entity; shareholders are taxed only upon distributions and deemed or actual capital gains in their own jurisdiction, subject to tax treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box classification regime. Available elective measures include (i) application for a Luxembourg VAT grouping regime (Groupe TVA) enabling affiliated taxable persons to be treated as a single taxable person; (ii) election for Luxembourg fiscal unity (consolidated corporate taxation) among directly or indirectly qualifying resident companies, including a SARL, subject to at least 95% joint control; (iii) the special alternative investment vehicle regimes and securitization regime elections; (iv) application for a bilateral APA and/or unilateral advance VAT clearances; and (v) anti-hybrid election mechanisms contained in Luxembourg's implementation of EU ATAD/ATAD II to reverse mismatches arising from hybrid financial instruments, hybrid entities, double inclusion income, and deductive/non-deductive arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax, taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold for taxable persons established in Luxembourg to benefit from the SME VAT exemption; non-established taxable persons and providers of strictly taxable supplies are required to register irrespective of turnover; distance sales of goods into Luxembourg exceed the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold to trigger Luxembourg VAT registration and compliance. For ISIC 5222 ship bunkering and refueling to international vessels, zero-rated supplies generally arise without reference to the domestic registration threshold, and the taxable person must hold a valid Luxembourg VAT number to issue compliant invoices and to support export and non-EU export claims.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates the use of structured e-invoicing for all B2G transactions routed through the PEPPOL network under the EU Directive 2014/55/EU; the Public Sector Invoice Management platform (eGP) is the receiving system. There is currently no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime for B2B invoices in Luxembourg. Taxpayers must preserve integrity of content, legibility, and audit trail; invoicing via EDI or EU-compliant structured PDF is permissible. For bunkering operations, the supply to a vessel must be evidenced by a bunker delivery note / delivraison de soutes report, which is not an e-invoice substitute but is a mandatory fiscal and customs substantiation document. Electronic reporting of the VAT return is performed through the AEDT MyGuichet portal; Intrastat and profiling data are filed separately where required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods and services qualifying as exports outside the European Union and, specifically, supplies of marine fuel (bunkers), lubricants, and ship provisions for vessels used in international navigation on the high seas are zero-rated under Luxembourg VAT law transposing EU VAT Directive Article 148 and implementing Article 66 of the Luxembourg VAT law. Eligibility requires the SARL to prove both the physical export from the EU customs territory and the economic nexus of the supply to the operation of an oceangoing vessel engaged in international trade. For ISIC 5222 marine bunkering, qualifying fuels/greases placed onboard a vessel undertaking a voyage to a non-EU port, an activity in international waters, or otherwise performing international transport of goods or persons, and which are delivered under a verifiable bunker delivery receipt, will be invoiced at 0% VAT. Exports of goods to non-EU jurisdictions require the vendor to obtain and keep positive proof of export including customs export declarations and transport documents. Offshore services performed from Luxembourg to owners/operators of non-EU vessels can also be zero-rated where the direct connection to the qualifying vessel and its international activity is evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document and/or electronic ECS/E-export notification) naming the SARL as exporter located in Luxembourg unless a deemed seller / triangulation arrangement applies
Bill of Lading or Seaway Bill or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing export out of the EU customs territory
Bunker Delivery Receipt (BDN) and physical quantity surveyor report demonstrating marine-fuel quantity supplied to the identified ocean-going vessel
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation showing settlement in the agreed payment rail (Swift Wire or Standby LC) from the foreign counterparty
Vessel particulars, IMO number, flag state certificate, voyage plan, and port clearance demonstrating the international voyage to/from a non-EU destination and absence of cabotage-only activity
Commercial invoice and signed delivery note cross-referenced to the BDN and vessel name
Contract of affreightment, charter party, or purchase order stating ISIC 5222 bunkering scope and international route
Intrastat declaration waiver or statement proving the goods have physically left the EU if routed through another Member State
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg AEDT, together with the Customs and Excise Administration, may retrospectively deny zero-rating and disallow input VAT deductions where export documentation is incomplete, fictitious, or fails to unambiguously establish physical removal from the EU and settlement from the foreign buyer. In the absence of robust BDN, customs, and FX repatriation evidence, the SARL is retroactively assessed at the Luxembourg standard VAT rate of 17% together with statutory late-interest charges and administrative penalties. In cases of proven fraud, criminal sanctions under the amended Luxembourg General Tax Law and VAT law can include imprisonment, public criminal fines, confiscation of assets, and permanent VAT registration derecognition. The ordinary reassessment period is three years from the end of the relevant VAT period, but in cases of bad faith or fraudulent conduct the clawback period may extend to ten years. The same penalties apply to any artificial arrangement, sham entity, or triangular scheme that seeks to zero-rate bunkers supplied to a vessel engaged exclusively in domestic or cabotage traffic rather than in genuine international trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., for 31 December YE: by 31 July the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers LBR reminder, then court-imposed penalty (astreinte) up to EUR 250/day (capped at EUR 10,000); persistent default can lead to administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: at least once per calendar year, within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing may result in criminal sanctions (Art. 16 RBE Law): imprisonment 6 months–3 years and/or fine EUR 10,000–1,250,000; additional per-day penalties after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax declaration (CIT + municipal business tax + net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline is normally 31 December of the following tax year (e.g., for 2024 financial year: due 31 December 2025, subject to granted extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 5,000; default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; possible assessment by tax office and criminal sanctions for gross default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies if any two of three thresholds are exceeded during two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, average headcount > 50. Small SARLs not exceeding these limits are exempt and may prepare simplified accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and on accounting); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for statutory accounts solely upon explicit election and for certain publicly traded entities; applicable for FY 2025.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any transfer of SARL shares must be recorded in the register of members. If the transfer causes a change in a beneficial owner (direct or indirect >25% interest), the RBE declaration must be updated within 30 days. Separately, all beneficial owner data must be re-confirmed annually via the RBE electronic platform within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial RBE filing, even if no change has occurred.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (fiscal year 2024 onward); aggregate effective mainstream rate in Luxembourg City is approximately 24.94%, comprising corporate income tax (CIT), a 4% solidarity surcharge on CIT, a 6% unemployment fund contribution on CIT, and deductible municipal business tax (IBT) at 6.75% (3% base rate × 225% multiplier).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No generic tax holidays exist for marine bunkering traders. Incentive levers: (i) 80% participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income; (ii) IP Box allowing 80% deduction of qualifying IP income (top effective rate 5.2%); (iii) 30% investment tax credit for qualifying fixed assets; (iv) tax-loss carry-forward without time bar. The tonnage tax regime is restricted to qualifying shipowners/operators and does not extend to a bunkering-only SARL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory temporal cap; carry-forward is forfeited where the beneficial ownership of the SARL changes by more than 50% in a break of legal continuity, and can be challenged under anti-abuse rules where losses are artificially monetized)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 510 (Déclaration d'impôt collectif) covering corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (IBT/NNA) and net wealth tax; filed electronically through the e-CDF module of MyGuichet.lu with a filing-institution token (délégation) for tax advisers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. One filing per fiscal year-end (calendar-year filing for nearly all SARLs). No quarterly CIT filing; preliminary CIT/IBT payments are due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the current year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutorily anchored deadline: 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY2024 return due 31 December 2025). Automatic extension to mid-subsequent year is granted for returns prepared and transmitted by a registered Luxembourg tax adviser; further prolongations de délai are available on reasoned request to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARL legal name, registered office, RCS number, Luxembourg matricule d'impôt, RBE beneficial-owner reference, and precise fiscal year start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident officers must be identified by name and country of residence; the SARL must disclose its permanent establishment in Luxembourg and the foreign tax residence of each beneficial owner for GAAR/directive screening.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit/loss before tax per the audited annual accounts, including bunkering turnover, cost of fuel sales, vessel-supply logistics costs, and financial income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile with the filed statutory financial statements of the Luxembourg SARL; foreign head-office allocations are inadmissible, and all revenue derived from Luxembourg operational decisions is attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment/entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and tax add-backs: disallowed entertainment costs, excessive director remuneration, non-deductible interest (earnings stripping), and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include intra-group management fees paid to a foreign affiliate without substance or adequate documentation; such fees are typically rejected in a non-resident-owner structure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions from the accounting result: carry-forward tax losses, municipal business tax (IBT) paid, participation-exempt income (dividends/capital gains) and IP-Box deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation exemption requires a qualifying 10% shareholding (or €1.2 million cost) held for at least 12 months; a non-resident parent must evidence the holding period and economic substance of the Luxembourg entity to retain the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base after adjustments; represents the consolidated base for CIT, net wealth tax (NWT) and municipal business tax (IBT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bunkering margins realized through the Luxembourg entity are fully taxable in Luxembourg; treaty-dependent profit allocation is irrelevant where the SARL is the resident principal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate computation column for municipal business tax applying the communal multiplier (e.g., 225% for Luxembourg City) on IBT taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SARL remains subject to IBT solely by virtue of registered office in the commune; no relief is granted for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E – Impôt sur le revenu des collectivités (Box 150–155)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computation at 17%, plus 4% solidarity surcharge and 6% unemployment contribution, after applicable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unilateral foreign tax credits are rarely relevant; treaty credits apply if the foreign state taxed the same bunkering income inconsistently with Luxembourg residency rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F – Impôt net à payer (Box 170-180)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT, IBT and NWT liability after preliminary payments, payable by bank transfer to the ACD's treasury account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advance payments made by the non-resident parent on behalf of the SARL must be formally recharacterized as shareholder loans or equity injections; unpaid declarations trigger ACD garnishment of the SARL's bank accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annexes – Transfer pricing and directive forms
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachment of Local File/Master File, intercompany agreement summaries, and any EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive forms used to claim reduced WHT on outbound dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A certificate of tax residence of the ultimate parent and proof of beneficial ownership must be attached; failure renders the combined filing materially incomplete.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes the SARL to taxation d'office on the inspector's own estimate, a late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on all unpaid CIT/IBT/NWT, and an administrative increase of up to 10% of the assessed tax under Article 176 LIR. Non-filing can additionally be prosecuted as fiscal negligence with fines of €25 to €250 per missing declaration and the revocation of the tax-adviser-filed deadline.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident shareholders, levied under Article 148 LIR; no solidarity surcharge is added to the 15% withholding. No WHT applies if the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption is satisfied (qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholder, minimum 10% holding, minimum 12-month holding at payment date).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief procedures: (i) for Directive exemption, the foreign corporate shareholder submits a completed Form 241 (tax-residence certificate from its state of residence and a beneficial-ownership affidavit) to the paying SARL before the dividend distribution; the Luxembourg ACD may require a prior letter-ruling or exemption certificate where anti-abuse doubts arise. (ii) Under double tax treaties, the recipient must file a certificate of residence (Form 210/211 series) plus documentary evidence of beneficial ownership; the ACD applies the relevant treaty ceiling (commonly 0% for participation holders, 15% for portfolio dividends) after verifying substance and the absence of a conduit arrangement. (iii) If withholding was applied at 15%, a refund claim can be lodged with the ACD within three years of the distribution, with interest awarded only in exceptional delayed-assessment cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory landscape: no Luxembourg withholding tax on royalties; no withholding tax on arm's-length interest paid by a corporate borrower to a non-resident lender, except the narrow 20% paying-agent levy under Article 148bis LIR (bearer-bond interest paid by a Luxembourg paying agent). Treaty outcomes: under most actively used DTA networks (United States, Germany, France, Netherlands), interest and royalties are exempt from Luxembourg source WHT at 0%, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits clauses; older or partial treaties occasionally reserve a 5–10% source right on certain cultural or industrial royalties. Excessive interest is subject to recharacterization under the interest-limitation rule (ATAD).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000 (cross-border related-party transactions exceeding this per fiscal year trigger the Local File obligation, provided the multinational group has consolidated turnover above EUR 50,000,000). The Master File must be maintained where the group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000 regardless of the local transaction volume; documentation must be delivered to the ACD within 15 days of an official demand (30 days with justified cause). Panama-style minimal margin resellers and back-to-back bunker supply arrangements are specific audit targets.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no codified Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the Gulf-Council sense, but substance is legally decisive through (i) the beneficial-ownership doctrine applied under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and DTAs, (ii) the EU ATAD GAAR (Article 6, in force since 1 January 2019), and (iii) settled Luxembourg case law denying treaty/directive benefits to letterbox entities. A bunkering SARL is expected to demonstrate real local direction: locally resident directors approving procurement/pricing, physical premises, qualified staff, local bank accounts, genuine risk-bearing, and commercial records evidencing actual bunker-supply decision-making. Absence of such substance invites reclassification of domicile, denial of the participation exemption, and re-source of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of bunkering income through false invoices, unrecorded fuel rebates, off-book cash or cryptocurrency settlement with marine clients/suppliers, fictitious deadfreight charges, or destruction of supply manifests to hide taxable margins.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment on the ACD's ex-officio basis; 10% administrative increase on the understated tax; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal prosecution under Articles 227–229 LIR with fines up to ten times the defrauded tax and imprisonment of one month to five years for the responsible natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally subject to criminal fines and imprisonment; civil liability for the full tax debt in case of fraudulent concealment; seizure of personal assets, professional disqualification, judicial travel bans, and in cross-border cases coordination with foreign tax authorities through administrative assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL as a brass-plate principal while the real bunkering business (procurement, risk, staff, and customers) is managed from a non-resident affiliate or the ultimate beneficial owner's home state, and channelling repatriation as exempt dividends without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the participation exemption and DTA/directive benefits; retroactive reclassification of foreign-managed income as taxable Luxembourg profit; 15% withholding tax (plus 0.6% monthly late interest) on deemed distributions; pecuniary penalties up to 10% of the reassessed tax; potential inclusion of the entity on the Luxembourg public list of abusive tax arrangements under DAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners may be held jointly liable for unpaid corporate taxes under veil-piercing jurisprudence and the Luxembourg criminal rules on misuse of corporate assets; travel bans and freezing orders are routinely issued in fraud-linked offshore conduit cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-volume cash, third-party or cryptocurrency payments from vessel operators without beneficial-owner KYC; using double-invoiced bunker supplies to launder proceeds; structuring false marine-fuel transactions to conceal the origins of funds linked to sanctioned shipping or smuggling networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT), as amended: administrative fines for legal persons up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; imprisonment of up to five years for implicated individuals; closure of bank accounts and revocation of the economic operator licence; the SARL's maritime-fuel licence can be suspended by the competent ministry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal prosecution, confiscation orders for laundered assets, travel bans, and exclusion from serving as managers of any regulated or licensed entity; civil liability extends to losses sustained by other creditors where the AML failure enabled dissipation of company assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating the bunkering margin through non-arm's-length back-to-back supply arrangements; allocating 0.5–1% routine returns to the Luxembourg SARL while profits accumulate in a zero-substance foreign affiliate; failure to prepare the Local File/Master File; absence of valid intercompany supply and logistics agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD upward adjustment of taxable profit under Article 56 LIR; additional municipal business tax and CIT; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; 10% surcharge on the reassessed tax; in egregious cases, criminal prosecution for false bookkeeping with fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed inaccurate TP documentation or intercompany pricing undertakings can be personally assessed for the additional tax if the SARL is insolvent; reckless or intentional mispricing supports civil fraud claims, director disqualification, and travel bans during cross-border tax investigation.
